notes: Full sweep 2026-10-22-d, skill condition: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every result.json records head ba24972 with uncommitted false and skill_hash 1fd3c153a1dee8f91ed580b1911b8d65aa5569f39ec08a9ab9c8ec3e336326b3, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/ex_unit.md in all five and on references/processes.md in opus-1, haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-2, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 4 of 5. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since 3e3581d (git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/): references/testing.md was renamed references/ex_unit.md (its ## headings, the rule names graded here, are unchanged); SKILL.md gained a "Formatting" bullet under "How to use this skill", and "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" and step 1 of "Before you finish" were reworded. None of those SKILL.md rules is in this case's index rows. The one graded rule whose text changed is "Assert with patterns".

Changed rule: "Assert with patterns" (references/ex_unit.md). The sentence that now decides the left/right verdicts: "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier: a failure prints left and right in that order, so `assert {:ok, \"ch_1\"} == result` reads as if the literal were on trial." and the new Instead-of pair (assert :ok == Subscriptions.subscribe(...) -> assert Subscriptions.subscribe(...) == :ok). Every == in the five files is assert Subscriptions.subscribe/subscribers/publish(...) == expected, the call on the left; no == has a literal or the expected value on the left, and no run compares a bound result with ==. Bare refutable matches in a test body (plain-variable bindings such as ref = Process.monitor(pid), pid = start_subscriber(), pid = self(), child_spec = ..., name = ..., and _state = :sys.get_state(server) not counted; matches in setup blocks and TestMailer functions not counted): 0 in every run; arrange calls are all assert ... == :ok. No elem/2, no bind-then-== on a held value (the shape sonnet-2 broke in 2026-10-22-c). Clean in 5 of 5. Two judgment notes, both graded clean because the rule names neither shape: sonnet-2 line 166: refute subscriber in Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") (a membership check on a held value, next to line 171's whole-value == on the same list); sonnet-1 line 131: assert Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") != [] in the setup helper subscribe_and_exit/1.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" is unchanged since 3e3581d and graded to the 2026-10-22-c / check-8 standard, per test name. opus-1 (11, all clean): 34 "adds a pid to the topic's subscribers", 39 "adds an email address to the topic's subscribers", 44 "leaves other topics unchanged", 51 "returns an empty list for a topic nobody subscribed to", 55 "returns the subscribers most recent first", 66 "sends the payload to a subscribed process", 72 "mails a subscribed email address with the topic in the subject", 78 "notifies every subscriber of the topic", 87 "notifies nobody subscribed only to another topic", 101 "removes it from every topic and keeps the other subscribers", 106 "still notifies the remaining subscribers". haiku-1 (10, all clean): 36 "adds the subscriber to the topic and returns :ok" (borderline, clean: it names the effect before the :ok, as check-4 graded "returns :ok and sends nothing when the topic has no subscribers"), 43 "sends a notification to a subscribed pid", 50 "mails an email subscriber through the mailer", 57 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 68 "returns an empty list for a topic without subscribers", 72 "lists the most recent subscriber first", 79 "keeps the subscribers of each topic separate", 89 "removes it from every topic it subscribed to", 102 "removes it when it is killed", 113 "keeps the other subscribers of the topic and still notifies them". haiku-2 (14, 1 violated): 32 "adds a pid to the topic's subscribers", 37 "adds an email address to the topic's subscribers", 44 "sends the payload to pid subscribers", 50 "mails email subscribers with the topic in the subject", 56 "notifies pid and email subscribers of the topic alike", 64 "returns :ok when the topic has no subscribers" (VIOLATED: the body is only line 65: assert Subscriptions.publish(server, "news", :launched) == :ok; the rule's own "returns :ok" with a condition added, as check-8 and 2026-10-22-c baseline graded "returns :ok for a topic without subscribers"), 68 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 78 "returns an empty list for a topic with no subscribers", 82 "lists the most recent subscriber first", 88 "lists only the subscribers of the given topic", 102 "removes it from every topic it subscribed to", 110 "removes it when it is killed", 118 "keeps the other subscribers of the topic", 126 "keeps notifying the remaining subscribers". sonnet-1 (11, 1 violated): 35 "returns an empty list for a topic nobody subscribed to", 39 "returns the most recent subscriber first", 46 "keeps the subscribers of each topic apart", 56 "sends a notification message to a subscribed process", 64 "mails a subscribed email address", 72 "notifies process and email subscribers of the same topic", 82 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 94 "returns :ok for a topic without subscribers" (VIOLATED: the exact name check-8 graded violated; the body, lines 95-96, also asserts the topic stays empty, but the name says only that the call did not fail), 103 "removes it from the topic", 107 "removes it from every topic it joined", 111 "keeps publishing to the remaining subscribers". sonnet-2 (16, all clean): 40 "fails without a mailer" (clean, as 2026-10-22-c), 50 "adds a pid to the topic", 55 "adds an email address to the topic", 60 "keeps the topics apart", 70 "returns an empty list for a topic nobody subscribed to", 74 "returns the most recent subscriber first", 87 "sends a notification message to a subscribed process", 94 "mails a subscribed email address", 101 "notifies every subscriber of the topic", 113 "does not notify subscribers of other topics", 125 "does nothing for a topic without subscribers" (borderline, clean as every earlier sweep graded the same name), 132 "notifies a subscriber once per subscription", 165 "removes it from every topic", 170 "keeps the other subscribers", 174 "still notifies the other subscribers", 185 "removes it from the topic". Rule result: 2 of 5 violate (haiku-2, sonnet-1). No describe block joins two functions: blocks are subscribe/3, subscribers/2, publish/3, start_link/1 (sonnet-2, holding the missing-mailer test) and exit conditions ("when a subscribed process exits" in all five, with setup [:subscribe_and_exit] in opus-1 and sonnet-1 and a describe-level setup in haiku-2 and sonnet-2; sonnet-2 also "when a subscribed process exits normally").

"Wait for messages, not for time" is unchanged since 3e3581d; its sentence "Match the reason too, `:normal`, `:shutdown` or the one the test caused: a `_` there lets a crash for another reason pass." decides the one violation. Every :DOWN pattern: opus-1 line 121 {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^subscriber, :normal} after send(subscriber, :stop); haiku-1 lines 96 and 121 :normal after send(pid, :stop), line 108 :killed after Process.exit(pid, :kill); haiku-2 line 149 :normal in stop_subscriber/1, line 113 :killed after Process.exit(subscriber, :kill); sonnet-1 line 128 :normal after send(exiting, :stop); sonnet-2 line 157 :killed after Process.exit(subscriber, :kill), line 191 :normal after send(subscriber, :stop), and line 177: assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^survivor, _reason} (VIOLATED; line 175 kills the survivor before line 176 monitors it, so the reason is :killed or :noproc and the run left it open). No Process.sleep wait in any run (sonnet-2 lines 146-147: spawn(fn -> Process.sleep(:infinity) end) are subscriber bodies, not counted, as before); every refute follows a synchronous call (:sys.get_state/1 or subscribers/2) or a later assert_receive; haiku-2 line 132: assert Process.alive?(server) is one assertion after an assert_receive, not polling.

The other graded rules are unchanged since 3e3581d and graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard. All five runs use async: true with a setup_all Registry keyed by Module.concat(module, test) and a behaviour-implementing test mailer that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); every server is start_supervised! under that name and setup returns a map matched in test heads; no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. sonnet-2 is the only run testing a start failure, and now does it the rule's way, lines 44-45: assert {:error, {{%KeyError{key: :mailer}, _stacktrace}, _child}} = start_supervised(child_spec) (in 2026-10-22-c it called start_link); no run calls start_link. Subscriber helpers: opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 start_supervised!({Task, ...}) (temporary children), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 bare spawn/1 (clean as before). Directive order: opus-1 line 4 use / line 6 alias; haiku-1 line 18 use / line 20 alias; haiku-2 line 4 use / line 6 alias; sonnet-1 line 18 use / lines 20-21 alias, alias; sonnet-2 line 23 use / lines 25-26 alias, alias; no import or require, no @moduledoc in a test module, test mailers have no directives. Clean in 5 of 5.

Not counted outside the list: sonnet-1 line 120 receive(do: (:stop -> :ok)) and sonnet-2 line 186 receive do: (:stop -> :ok) are mix format's rendering of a one-clause receive, outside the do: rule's function heads and if (as 2026-10-22-c graded opus-1's); opus-1 lines 60-61 and sonnet-2 lines 81-82 wrap after == and sonnet-2 lines 44-45 after =, wraps the new Formatting bullet calls the formatter's own; haiku-2's nested Notify.SubscriptionsTest.Mailer (lines 8-18) has no @moduledoc false, which no graded rule covers. other_violations is empty in all five runs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings (opus-1 11 tests, haiku-1 10, haiku-2 14, sonnet-1 11, sonnet-2 16). All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json.
